To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

traffic aided opportunistic schedulers can achieve a significant performance gain over opportunistic schedulers that are unaware of file size and channel variation information, and that the performance gain is particularly prominent when the arrival rate of users is high.
the proposed TA OS schemes can reduce the total completion times by 10%-30% compared to the conventional opportunistic scheduling schemes.

(i) the total completion time is minimized when the file sizes and channels are perfectly known, and the optimal policy is a greedy policy, (ii) the TAOS schemes perform very well when the arrival and departure processes are random, and (iii) when the arrival rate becomes very high, TAOS schemes perform better than the greedy scheme.

the problem of reducing the completion times of users in multiuser wireless networks.
the design of opportunistic scheduling schemes that take advantage of the file size and channel variation information to reduce the system completion time.
